name: Wavefolded LFO wobble: fold a sine LFO for extra peaks/valleys, then slew-limit it before filter cutoff
goal: Make complex but smooth filter wobbles by running a plain sine LFO through a wavefolder (fold amount, symmetry, fold shape add peaks and valleys) before it reaches filter cutoff, then put a slew limiter after the folder so the folded modulation is less jumpy — a modulation-shaping recipe distinct from audio-rate wavefolding.

source.title: Wavefolding LFO's in VCV Rack to make interesting wobble effects and unique waves Synth Sound Design

prerequisites: LFO, wavefolder accepting a control signal (Web Audio: WaveShaperNode on an LFO signal, implementation note), slew limiter / one-pole smoother, filter

outputs.name: wobble_filter
outputs.description: Filter moved by a folded, slewed LFO

constraints: Original synthesis recipe; not affiliated with any vendor named in the source. Recreate in browser/Web Audio (Polyrhythm Studio) or any hybrid synth with comparable modules; no presets, banks or samples copied.
Transcript is short (≈380 words); amounts are by ear, no numeric settings given.
Folded LFO at fast rates becomes jumpy — slow it down or slew it.

steps.action: Baseline: route a regular sine LFO to filter cutoff and listen.
Insert a wavefolder between LFO and filter cutoff; compare the folded and plain sine on a scope.
steps.expect: Folded sine shows extra peaks and valleys; wobble becomes more complex

steps.action: Slow the LFO down (folding multiplies apparent rate) and adjust fold amount, symmetry and fold shape.
steps.expect: Different repeating wobble patterns per setting

steps.action: Add a slew limiter after the wavefolder, before the cutoff input, to soften the jumps.

verification: Scope shows more peaks per cycle after the folder than before.
Increasing slew audibly smooths jumps without removing the extra contour.
